bots.title: Bots
bots.about: Reusable model tasks: a prompt, MCP servers, skills and project files — run by hand or on a schedule. Each bot is a bots/name.md file in the project: you see it in «Files» and in git.
bots.example_hint: A bot that finds Jira issues with a label, looks up Confluence pages, evaluates by a template, attaches a file and adds a comment. The evaluation template goes to templates/ if missing.
bots.example_made: The example is created — check the label in the prompt and switch the schedule on
bots.example_made_tpl: The example is created, the evaluation template is {tpl}
bots.empty: No bots yet. Create your own or start from the example.
bots.pick: Pick a bot on the left or create a new one.
bots.failed: It did not work — details are in the log
bots.leave_ask: The bot has unsaved edits. Leave without them?
bots.description_ph: In short: what the bot does
bots.run_hint: Run the bot now: progress is in the «Console», the outcome below
bots.running: The bot is working… progress is in the «Console»
bots.run_bad: The bot failed — the reason is below
bots.rename_hint: Name the bot file after its name (bots/name.md)
bots.delete_ask: Delete the bot «{name}» ({file})? The file leaves the project; it stays in the git history.
bots.prompt_hint: What the bot does. Attachments can be named by a link — the «Insert link» button next to an attachment.
bots.mode_hint: Editor view — the same as in «Files»
bots.mcp_about: Connected right away; the bot sees no other servers.
bots.mcp_none: No MCP servers. They are added in «Kit setup» → machine MCP servers or in the project's mcp.json.
bots.skills_about: Their method (SKILL.md) goes into the bot's task.
bots.attachments_about: Project files and folders — as references, not copies. At run time their text goes to the bot, and it can read them in full.
bots.insert_link_hint: Insert a link to the attachment into the prompt — at the cursor
bots.cron_about: A bot with the schedule on appears in the «Cron» section by itself.
bots.cron_format: minute hour day month weekday: 0 9 * * 1-5 — weekdays at 9:00; or @daily, @weekly
bots.next_runs_off: Switch it on and the runs will be: {list}
bots.add_to_cron_hint: Switch the schedule on (if none — weekdays at 9:00) and save
bots.added_to_cron: The bot is scheduled: next run {when}
bots.fix.no_bot: Check the file name in the bots/ folder.
bots.fix.no_prompt: Write the prompt in the file body.
bots.fix.cron_invalid: Five fields: minute, hour, day, month, weekday — e.g. 0 9 * * 1-5; or a preset from the list.
bots.p.mcp_unknown: The MCP server is not set up
bots.fix.mcp_unknown: Add it in «Kit setup» → machine MCP servers (or the project's mcp.json) or untick it.
bots.fix.skill_unknown: Put SKILL.md into the project's .claude/skills/<name>/, the kit's skills/ or ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ — or untick it.
bots.p.attachment_missing: The attachment is not in the project
bots.fix.attachment_missing: The path is from the project root: fix it or remove the attachment.
bots.p.attachment_secret: The attachment is secrets or a service folder
bots.fix.attachment_secret: Such files are not given to a bot: remove the attachment.
bots.fix.no_models: The «Models» section: a provider and a backend for the «Writer: parsing, theses, answers» role.
bots.p.no_adapter: No Pydantic AI — the bot will have no MCP servers and tools
bots.fix.no_adapter: Install Pydantic AI on the «Install» page.
bots.p.timeout: The bot ran out of time
bots.fix.timeout: Shorten the task (e.g. one label per run) or raise the request timeout and budget in the «Models» section.
bots.p.tool_limit: The bot used up its tool calls
bots.fix.tool_limit: Split the task — e.g. one label per bot — or run it more often.
bots.fix.model_failed: Check the connection in the «Models» section; if the server is overloaded, retry later.
bots.role_about: A role from the «Models» section: a «provider → model» chain in order. You can add a role of your own for bots, with a stronger model.
bots.fix.role_unknown: Pick a role from the «Models» section or add it there.
bots.fix.no_tools: The call bypassed Pydantic AI — no MCP servers and files. The reason is in the report; check Pydantic AI on the «Install» page.
bots.fix.no_tool_calls: The bot's MCP servers were connected, but the model answered with text. Say in the prompt which tool to call first (e.g. the Jira issue search), or pick a role with a stronger model.
bots.group_roles: Roles — by their chain, with spares
bots.fix.model_unknown: A model is set as «provider/model», the provider being from the «Models» section. Pick it in the «Model» card or set a role.
bots.knowledge_about: Before work the bot gets a knowledge pack, like “Productivity”: the task's links → concepts → Aurora's hybrid search in the chosen project's base. During work it searches the same base itself.
bots.p.knowledge_unknown: There is no such knowledge project
bots.fix.knowledge_unknown: Pick a project in the “Project context” card — from the panel's projects — or keep its own.
bots.context.evaluate: Pack: all knowledge, with trust marks
bots.context.off: No pack — the bot searches itself
bots.coach.hint: A conversation with a model about the prompt: what will run, what will not, which tools are missing, what is extra; edits on your request
bots.coach.title: Prompt review with AI
bots.coach.about: The model relies on the engine's facts: the bot's real tools (with descriptions from the servers themselves), signs of scripts, environment variables and direct requests, the time limit and the call limit. A new prompt goes into the editor and is not saved by itself — “Save” at the top.
bots.coach.model_hint: What to review with: a role (a chain with spares) or exactly a provider model
bots.coach.refresh_hint: Ask the bot's MCP servers for their tools again — with the next message
bots.coach.refresh_next: I will ask the servers for their tools again with the next message
bots.coach.reset_ask: Forget the conversation and review the prompt again?
bots.coach.first: The model is reviewing the prompt. Reasoning models answer in minutes; you can close the window — the answer is kept in the conversation.
bots.coach.thinking: The model is thinking… you can close the window — the answer is kept in the conversation.
bots.coach.changed: the model returned a new prompt
bots.coach.applied: The new prompt is in the editor. Check it and save
bots.coach.undo_hint: The prompt was replaced by the model's answer.
bots.coach.ph: Ask or request a change: “rewrite step 2 with jira_search”, “remove the extra servers”…
bots.coach.send_hint: Ctrl+Enter — send. The conversation is about what is in the editor now.
bots.coach.q.rewrite: Rewrite the prompt so that every step is done with the bot's available tools: replace scripts, environment variables and direct requests with tools, and remove or mark what cannot be done. Return the whole new prompt.
bots.coach.q.trim: Which of the bot's servers and tools will not be called with this prompt? Suggest removing extra servers (a META line) and shorten the prompt without losing meaning. Return the whole new prompt.
bots.coach.q.missing: Which tools are missing for the bot to do the task fully? What to connect from the available servers, and what exists nowhere — and what to do then?
bots.coach.q.risks: What are the risks of this unattended run: writing into external systems, the time limit, the call limit, trial and live mode, repeated runs? What to fix in the prompt?
bots.coach.reapply_hint: Put the prompt from this answer into the editor; the current one can be brought back
